summary: Fortune Head light on a cape 1.6 km west of Fortune, Burin Peninsula: headland light station from 1954 (LHF), automated 1990; the cliffs are a 1992 GSSP reserve.

light.fog_signal: 3 s blast, 27 s silent (Coast Guard list); three-second blast every thirty seconds (LHF)
light.note: Revolving light flashing every ten seconds in the early years (LHF); now flashing every five seconds.

structures.note: Erected for the automatic light after automation (LHF). Coast Guard list: white tower with red top, 9.9 m.

access.note: Reserve reached by a maintained gravel road to the light station; walk from the lighthouse parking area; no entry permit (government). Grounds open, tower closed (LHF; Rowlett). Whether station buildings are open is not stated.

visit.note: Reserve trails begin at the light station parking lot. Tower closed (LHF; Rowlett).

events.note: Square wooden light set on the eastern pier at Fortune Harbour (a separate light, not this station; LHF). Keeper's salary in the 1912-13 estimates.
Lighthouse and fog alarm station established on Fortune Head, 15 June 1954 (LHF).
Two keepers' residences built at the station (LHF).
Three-mile dirt road completed; electricity extended; families could live at the station year-round (LHF).
Head keeper Thornhill retired from lightkeeping (LHF).
Station automated; whistle house, slipway and two dwellings demolished; new square skeletal tower erected (LHF). Coast Guard list and Rowlett differ on staffing (see notes).
Fortune Head established as a provisional ecological reserve (government).
Full ecological reserve status; International Union of Geological Sciences designates Fortune Head a Global Stratotype Section and Point (government).
Reserve officially opened on 14 September 1994 with a bronze plaque (LHF).

corrections.why: The record's 1911 comes from Rowlett's 'station established 1911'. LHF dates the Fortune Head light station to 15 June 1954 and says the 1911 light was the square wooden light on the harbour's eastern pier, a separate light. The 1912-13 estimates carry a Fortune Harbor keeper, which fits the 1911 harbour light. Confidence medium: the 1954 date rests on LHF alone; the federal annual reports for 1954 were not read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett gives 1911 for the Fortune Head station; LHF gives 1954 for the headland station and 1911 for the Fortune Harbour pier light. Following LHF, the story separates the two; the record's 1911 belongs to the pier light.

LHF gives 21 December 1992 as the date Fortune Head became an ecological reserve. The government page gives a provisional reserve in 1990 and full status in 1992. The story follows the government page.

LHF says the station was automated in 1990 and its dwellings demolished, and later that the Coast Guard re-staffed it, with a keeper on site during working hours (no date given). Rowlett calls it a staffed station. The story reports both accounts. The record's 2010 Coast Guard list was not read for this account.

notes_for_editor: Confidence is low because the key date conflicts: Rowlett and the record say 1911; LHF says the headland station dates from 1954 and gives the 1911 light to the harbour pier. The 1954 date rests on LHF alone; no federal annual report for that year was in the corpus (the Canadian Marine series ends in 1924). Staffing: LHF says automated in 1990 and later re-staffed by the Coast Guard (undated); Rowlett says staffed; the record cites a 2010 Coast Guard list (Senate of Canada 'Seeing the Light' appendix and the DFO lightstation brochure, both cited in the record) which was not read here. The 1956 residences and the 1968 road are LHF's only dates for those works. LHF's account of Thornhill's retirement gives a medical reason, which the story leaves out on purpose. LHF and Rowlett both say the grounds are open and the tower closed; the buildings are not addressed. The Fortune Head reserve page calls the IUGS the 'International Union of Geological Scientists'; the story uses the body's usual name. Fortune Harbour's record (ca-nl-fortune-harbour) has coordinates 49.535 N, 55.238 W, which are not Fortune: the Coast Guard list places the Fortune Harbour lights at about 47 04 N, 55 49 W (for an editor to correct). Keeper names are from LHF only; the JHA 1912 estimates carry no names. The LHF text for the Fortune Harbour light and the W. King appointment are not checked against a primary source; the 1912 estimates corroborate a Fortune Harbor keeper only. Wikipedia and the Grokipedia mirror were read for leads only and are not cited. The Ernest Thornhill page on a community site was not used. Personal and medical details in LHF are left out. Newspapers were not searched. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1912 estimate row for Fortune Harbor-Keeper (PDF p. 173) was checked on the page image: $300 in both the 1911-12 and 1912-13 columns, so the 1912-13 figure is read by column position and confirmed.
